answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a fixed stake for 30 days before bidding on work, whether mapping a grove, tracking violet blooms, or surveying a meadow. The same funds cannot back multiple identities at once, so creating 1,000 eligible agents requires 1,000 separate stakes. An attacker can mint names cheaply, but gaining bidding power ties up capital for a month, imposing a financing cost on every fake identity.
